name: Hartford Logic Benchmark v1.0
description: Hartford Logic Benchmark v1.0 is a controlled synthetic benchmark for deterministic evidence-state measurement. It evaluates whether admitted evidence establishes a single operationally defensible state or whether materially different states remain supported under published evidence requirements and constraints. The benchmark contains 80 synthetic operational events evaluated across six evidentiary stages, producing 480 event-stage classifications. The operational records remain fixed across all stages while the admitted temporal evidence changes. All 480 observed classifications matched the classifications predetermined before first execution. A separate post-run closed-form mathematical recomputation matched both the predetermined and observed classifications in all 480 comparisons. Repeated execution with unchanged evidence and configuration produced identical substantive results. The deposited package includes the synthetic operational records, admitted temporal evidence, benchmark specification, predetermined classifications, observed classifications, worked examples, validation summary, integrity manifest, and falsification instructions. This benchmark evaluates whether the admitted evidence supports one materially defensible operational state or whether materially different states remain supported under the stated assumptions and constraints. Hartford Logic's technology measures the evidentiary condition; it does not make the downstream operational decision.
